It is a deliberately wide editorial scenario. Neither the anime nor the short farming passage provides a canonical national participation census.

after.description:

This is retained as an interpretive zero variant: automation can remove production jobs while access and bargaining power remain unequal. The weak guarantee score is an editorial reading of that relationship, not a claim that the manga supplies a comprehensive national welfare code. Human careers and informal work remain important.

Companies and state institutions hold concentrated productive power; networked minds do not automatically create either a commons or an autonomous AI government. The modest nonworking estimate allows displacement and dependents while counting embodied cyborg activity, care and technical service as real human-derived work. It does not classify a worker as a machine merely because the body is artificial. The scope is deliberately the original manga, since the scholarly excerpt distinguishes its overt labor dialogue from the film’s different emphasis.

The best-guess material reading is a partly machine-supported city that gives recognized residents a conditional floor, while making exclusion and official approval consequential. The guarantee score is therefore moderately favorable but uncertain. A moderately high nonworking estimate allows broad technical support while retaining useful administration, care, maintenance and security work. It is not a claim that residents only consume. The record stops before the city’s destruction and does not count dead residents as leisure citizens or assume that all domes follow identical rules.

A moderate nonworking estimate allows substantial displacement and machine assistance while retaining useful human care, services, science and administration. Neither a robot’s presence nor an unaffordable purchase supplies an exact labor statistic. The point remains a transparent editorial comparison across the shared premise.

scope.period: The functioning city before the final attempted purge
scope.population: Living human and biological Bioroid residents

after.description:
Olympus is a technologically sustained city administered through a technocratic order in which Gaia, officials and biological Bioroids all matter. The best-guess admission is a partly automated urban provision system with relatively strong resident support. The film’s advanced infrastructure makes that plausible, but a complete universal entitlement package is not stated. Guarantees retain a wide interval because the political conflict exposes how dependent ordinary life is on decisions made at the center.

Control is placed near concentrated humanlike authority, with a broad range toward machine coordination and shared civic influence. Gaia’s presence alone does not settle who ultimately controls production. Bioroids are biological persons performing useful administrative and other work, not a robot workforce that can be erased from participation. The nonworking estimate therefore stays moderate despite technological abundance. It includes dependents and people freed from routine production while counting care, governance, security and research. Other manga and film continuities are not automatically assigned the same economic model.
